text:
sre-alerts-bot: ALERT: hosted-inference.gateway: p99 latency SLO burn and 5xx spike detected (5m window). 5xx rate = 3.2%, p99 = 1.8s. Alert ID: HI-GW-20260315-01.

sre-alerts-bot: Related metrics -> https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/hosted-infer/gateway-overview

julia: seeing a handful of support tickets complaining about repeated 504s and client-side timeouts. one customer says they hit this when sending batch of long prompts (seq_len ~ 4k).

matt: I can confirm traces show a pattern: request makes it to gateway, then gateway never emits a downstream span to inference-pool for ~60% of failed requests. looks like a connection/tcp handoff sometimes never completes.

lee: interesting — are we seeing TLS handshake spikes or just backend accept failures? I pulled tcp_metrics: `tcp_connect_time` for gpu-pool shows 95p up ~200ms -> 800ms in the window. that's big.

ana: reproduced locally with a small script: `for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @payload.json; done` -> ~15% 504 with identical payloads.

julia: customer reports also saw intermittent 502s with message 'upstream prematurely closed connection'.

matt: logs query I ran (loki): `{job=\"gateway\"} |= \"504\" |= \"upstream prematurely\" | json | count_over_time(5m)` returned 310 in last 5m.

lee: tracing gap seems correlated with a specific AZ and a single model shard group: inference-pool-eu-west-2b-02. fallback traffic to other shards reduces errors.

support-bot: Support ticket #98741 linked: customer env id=acct-3345. They reported timeouts starting ~2026-03-15T08:58Z.

julia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) open incident, 2) enable routing-fallback to other shard groups for affected customers, 3) increase connection pool retry timeout from 250ms -> 1s temporarily, 4) kick off targeted autoscale for the suspect shard.

matt: config snippet to enable fallback routing (apply to routing service):
```
routing_rules:
  - match: {region: eu-west-2, model: *}
    action: fallback_to: [inference-pool-eu-west-2a-01, inference-pool-eu-west-2c-01]
    max_retries: 2
    retry_backoff_ms: 100
```

lee: I'm worried about hidden auth/billing failures too — I saw a pattern where auth-proxy returns 200 but connection closed immediately if token introspection times out. can we check KMS introspect and our auth cache hit rate?

ana: quick queries: auth-proxy logs show increased latency in introspect RPCs to auth-db: `introspect_latency_ms p99 = 420ms` during the window (baseline 30ms). ticketing shows auth-db CPU bump on that host.

julia: action items assigned: matt -> investigate gateway->pool connection handshake logs and open a host-level folder. lee -> verify auth-proxy caches and whether token spikes correlate with specific customers. ana -> run a canary traffic shift for acct-3345 to alternate shard and observe. i'll coordinate comms with support.

matt: hypothesis: an autoscaler bug recently deployed caused transient pod churn on that shard group, leaving some gateway connections to half-open states. looking at deploys: `deploy-service inference-pool` had a canary at 2026-03-15T08:45Z.

lee: can we quickly run a Grafana panel with connection reset metrics and view `gateway.tcp.reset_count` aggregated by backend shard? linking below.

julia: temporary workaround rolled out: increased gateway connection timeout to 10s and enabled fallback-rules for the affected shard group. monitoring alert thresholds lowered to catch recurrence.

support-bot: Support update: Customer acct-3345 notified of mitigation and asked to retry. awaiting confirmation.

matt: follow-up: I collected tcpdump from gateway->inference for a failed request; shows SYN, SYN-ACK then RST from backend after ~350ms with no TLS ClientHello (handshake aborted). saving pcap to s3://redwood-internal/pcaps/1765432100.pcap

lee: next steps: 1) correlate deploys and k8s restarts on that shard group 2) validate autoscaler bugfix (rolling patch ready) 3) add circuit-breaker to avoid endless half-open retries 4) run a guided repro with lower concurrency to verify fix.

julia: created incident: INC-20260315-01 (priority P1) and assigned oncall. tagging eng-runtime and infra teams. please add any useful links to the incident doc.

ana: confirm — after fallback rules and timeout tweak we saw 5xx drop from 3.2% -> 0.6% in 10m. will keep monitoring.

julia: thank you all. I'll own postmortem owner. please add logs/pcaps/traces to the incident page. :eyes: :thumbsup:

sre-alerts-bot: RESOLVED: initial SLO burn suppressed by routing fallback and connection timeout adjustments. Monitoring will auto-close if no regression in 30m.
